answers.answer: Roll one die simultaneously for each held office card, add one per fatigue and one more for the Chairman: modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this attrition roll.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. They act by descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards while selecting; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard every card left and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected a card. Return unused Pensioners to supply.

At phase start, check the opportunity marker; a player may take a main action twice only if the marker already matched that action. Then move the marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law can give an extra action, which is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer adds one additional writer once that turn: if the marker already matches Writer, two main-action placements plus the one-time extra writer bonus means three writers total.

After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants exist, move the rightmost Stock Exchange applicant into Court as a Company share and lower Debt one; repeat. If no Debt remains, move the remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Seeking a share paid its listed queue cost (£2, £3, £3, £4, or £5) to the bank; it did not pay family cash into Company treasuries.

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate; the candidate moves into the office and its owner gets the office card. Promoting an officeholder transfers their fatigue to the new card and inserts the old card as vacant in ascending order. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman first states how many shares make a pure majority (more than half the current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares to the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece remains a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If no one wins support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent.

For a Company-office check, commit any required resources and pay its cash from that acting office's treasury to the bank; gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office limits permit, while 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its holder to supply, discards fatigue and flips its card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success (examples: trading with no ship or deploying with no dice to trigger losses).

The Chairman may freely add up to three Debt, gaining £5 Balance per advance. Each additional advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting; never advance beyond the Debt track end. Allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved within those rules; cash already in office treasuries stays available to those offices.

The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury cash until £2 or less remains. They may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without its owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship goes in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

Declare the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. A President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: first writer goes to home port; each later order must touch a writer placed in this same Presidency's Trade, not another Presidency's writer. Use actual writers then filled tokens. No President fills another President's home region, even if vacant. Company receives printed order value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; President gets £1 per order and writer owners £1 per writer. Dividers separate adjacent writers of different Presidencies for Refresh.

Deploy may target the Commander's own Presidency home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give the action an effect. Exhaust chosen officers/regiments for one die each and alliances for their printed dice; subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire (count target once; Company defense strength is zero), then roll. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss checks. Noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources.

Successful Deploy loot is £4 per target tower plus its faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to surviving officers used in that attempt plus one for the Commander. Count only this attempt's surviving participating officers and used regiments/alliances. Distribute repeatedly in cycles: £1 to Commander first (plus £1 per their used surviving officer), then clockwise £1 per other family's used surviving officer, then bank £1 per used regiment and per alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength; repeat until loot is exhausted. Commander takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome (and all matching flags if capital), open all orders and clear unrest. If newly conquered, put the control token region-side up above associated President, Governor overlay on map, and office card in Vacant Offices; Governor General means no new Governor/overlay. Move an outward-facing Elephant fully inside the conquered region. Catastrophe instead returns half the Commander's family's trophies rounded up and the Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.

Governor starts with the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. A success pays £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: build a ship one stage (first success places partial ship in region; a later success completes it into the associated sea zone), commission a regiment into associated Army (officer-like strength, loot to bank, no officer-loss rolls), or tax £2 unsplit into Company Balance or President's treasury. Each tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes holder. Repeat until stopping, no dice, or catastrophe.

Revenue first charges £1 per existing Debt, each Army officer/regiment and each sea-zone ship (including China; not Commanders). If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one at a time; loans continue even at maximum Debt. Newly added Debt does not add a current-turn expense. After loans, set Balance to zero; one or two loans lower Standing one, three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing; if lower, reduce Standing one. Then Chairman may pay any affordable dividends, one cash per Company share and £1 to each owner per share including Chairman. If total dividend cash strictly exceeds expectations, raise Standing one. Standing at leftmost is failure.

A Crisis at the Elephant attacks the region at its head from its tail. For attacks on Company, resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in every other unrest Company region in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses region order. Primary normal Crisis strength is its normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only the ordinary attack die; each secondary Rebellion uses only that region's unrest cubes. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling attack strength, or as many as possible; local alliance strength counts and cannot be split. Printed defense rule says defense succeeds only if newly exhausted pieces equal Crisis strength; then clear all unrest and give Commander a trophy, plus remove an attacker tower if this was a successfully defended normal primary Invasion. A vacant Commander is replaced for defense by Military Affairs, or Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; they choose pieces but gain/lose no trophies. Excess indivisible-alliance strength is unresolved in this summary. If primary Company attack succeeds, apply empire growth.
answers.evidence: Events—Attacks on Company; FAQ source gap

answers.answer: PM draws at least one law. After one or two ordinary laws they may stop or continue to at most three, then choose one revealed law. A dilemma forces selection immediately and ends drawing. Before voting, PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching the law's bottom icon, which fixes target/consequence, then sets support to printed starting value. At resolution, support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial, new PM shifts proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves it. Support 0 or more passes: put law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects. Restore rotated vote cards after either outcome. Complete vote if law causes failure, then score.

In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses ordinary vote procedure and threshold with these exceptions: passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM a passed-law token and activates firms; no policy accompanies it. Failure raises Company share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token (maximum ±3); it does not remove PM or discard the Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated; 1710 has no Deregulation procedures.

To form a firm, a player who manages none contributes one eligible Company share (returned to supply) or flips a workshop to invested, flips family board to firm charter, places a family member as first share, sets value to leftmost, and takes £5 from bank to London treasury. To invest in a firm, get manager consent and contribute a Company share/workshop similarly; bank supplies £5 to London treasury. Up to ten shares can be created; beyond that contributions still give £5 but no share. Chairman share cannot be used; no Company shares may be used while Standing and/or Debt is lined, and shares created this turn cannot be reinvested even if traded away. Invested workshops stay invested and lose workshop bonus and Company-failure VP. London funds investments/ship acquisition/trade bids/expenses; India receives trade and funds dividends/expenses. Family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt each turn. Managers secretly choose a trade zone/home port (must have a ship; a closed home port is allowed) and London-cash bid, or Hobnob (no bid, trade or dividends). Reveal bids together, but strategies remain facedown until matching Presidency starts. Then reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, pay bid to bank; any 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. President's successful Trade creates initiative by same method. After President success, fill lowest initiative first; President chooses tied order. If President vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governors, with Chairman breaking ties. Each fills up to ships+1 open orders from home port through its own route, each order at most once per firm. They can refill others' orders; Company can refill firms' orders. Filled tokens yield trade revenue to India treasury; orders already filled this turn pay half listed amount rounded down. Advance Value one per full £6 added to India treasury that turn.

At Revenue start, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, from London and/or India treasuries. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, charter flips to family side, and invested workshops stay invested. Rescue by emergency investment follows normal contribution rules even at ten-share cap; pay expenses, lose any remaining rescue cash, and lower Value one per investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which first pays its own expenses if needed and covers the endangered firm's shortfall. After expenses manager may pay dividends from India treasury only: each pays £1 per share plus £1 manager. A shareholder may waive any number of shares only with manager consent. Record total actual cash paid out on Company Balance track; active non-Hobnob firm with no dividend records zero, Hobnob retains marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.

Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Components otherwise are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible; cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids temporarily concealed during selection.

Negotiations may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Cannot transfer officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial, or Chairman piece. When a share transfers, replace the member with new owner's family piece; adjust VP when luxury changes owner. Blackmail may be shown privately but never traded faceup; once used and faceup it cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; promises about future behavior are not, except a printed promise card can force its guaranteed effect if possible. Promise cards can be traded to a third party or back to guarantor. If several simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Follow each card's timing/limits; transferred resources cannot activate twice. No promise calls or negotiations during Final Scoring.

For five players add three extra scenario player setup cards; for six add six. Shuffle and deal evenly, then take listed cash, enterprises and positions. Put office family member in office and matching office card with owner; Company share member in Court; writers/officers/trainees in listed boxes; Commander in Army slot without office card; ship and shipyard as listed, ship in specified sea zone or on yard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together and deal three London display cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown); shuffle remaining laws and distinguish vacant from uncreated office cards.

Game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. If failure occurs during Revenue, go directly to Final Scoring; if during Events in India, finish that phase first; if legislation causes failure, finish the vote first. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; no negotiations or promise calls during Final Scoring.

Total Power from enterprises/shares at current track (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power (blackmail faceup or facedown, applicable spouse). First/second awards are turns 1–3: 3/1 VP; turns 4–6: 5/2; turns 7–8: 8/4. A tied-first group each receives only the lower award, with no second award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins; ties break by most windows, then clockwise from PM.

If Company survives, each Company share adds its current Court VP value. If it fails, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop; invested workshops give no failure VP. On survival, roll office attrition and retire pensioners without prestige cards. On failure, draw and resolve a random Company failure card instead. Deregulated firm scoring and special retirement occur before these normal steps and regardless of Company failure.

Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades occur immediately when taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each can be used once during a London Season and once during Final Scoring; they reduce actual spending and thus prestige selection priority. Firm special retirements can use spouse discounts to afford a higher printed-cost prize.

When a shipyard returns because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. The shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; purchase can occur after that ship returns to the shipyard.

Enlist Writer: place member in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices place one extra writer once that turn. Enlist Officer: place member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to bank; gains luxury, 2 VP while owned and window icon (social enterprise). Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to bank; take yard and matching ship unfitted on it (shipping enterprise, one vote, £1 bonus while fitted). Purchase Workshop costs £5 to bank; manufacturing, two votes, £1 bonus, and 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share costs the empty queue space price £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 to bank and places applicant; it may become Company share only after Family phase as Debt is reduced. No cash costs are stated for enlisting.

If a family member must be placed and none is in supply, take one from any of that family's prizes and lose that prize's printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, taking one from a prize and losing that prize's VP. If this is impossible (no supply piece and no prize piece available), there is no Chairman.

Chairman chooses Director from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices are vacant, any writer. Chairman chooses Manager of Shipping from any writer and Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, or if none any officer, or if none any trainee. Director chooses each President from writer or Governor associated with that Presidency. Associated President chooses Governor from writer or officer in region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. Chairman chooses China Superintendent from any writer and hires immediately when created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. Ordinary own-family hire needs consent from every other player in candidate pool; Chairman and Commander appointments are exempt.

Director can make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 of treasury per die with no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and having Chairman immediately hire a writer. After completing all envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, one writer or ship each between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created). Transfers cannot occur while taking envoys.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers of one officer/regiment between Armies, leaving them in the top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army's top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or a family has more total pieces in Army than incumbent's family, choose among families with most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot and return old Commander to top half as officer. Tie with incumbent's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President sets order for its Commander, Governors and its own Trade; each position gets an opportunity, but Commander/Governors may decline. Each position completes its actions before next, and Trade may be before or after any but cannot interrupt one. A President cannot interrupt a position's own failed/retried checks. If President is vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Trade ships do not become exhausted as a result of trade. During Refresh, return writers to their associated Presidencies; return filled-order tokens and Presidency dividers; return extra ships to supply. Player-fitted ships retain fatigue.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Upkeep and Refresh: writers/tokens/dividers/extra ships; no explicit trade-ship exhaustion statement

answers.answer: Before Deploy, Commander requests President's treasury funds for local alliances at printed price; President must approve. Purchased alliances go to top/active half. Using one for Deploy or defense exhausts the whole alliance to bottom; its printed strength can be used once that turn and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too; it does not reactivate alliances like officers/regiments. The summary does not otherwise specify a general procedure to split alliance strength.

In an already Company-controlled region targeted to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero, and because no tower remains there are zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot is the minimum of surviving participating officers plus £1 for Commander, distributed normally. Deployment still requires a possible check and uses its regular dice/resource rules; there is no further special dice penalty stated for this case.
answers.evidence: Deploying in an already Company-controlled region

answers.answer: Building a Company ship takes two successful Administer choices: the first success places a partial ship in the Governor's region if none is there; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. A partial ship otherwise has no effect. Governor-commissioned regiments go in the Army associated with Governor's President; they have officer-like strength, pay loot to bank, and do not roll officer-loss checks.

China is created by a successful Director Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may send ships there as to any sea zone. China acts after Bengal. China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

China may attempt Trade once after Bengal, rolling one die per ship, only if Company regions have at least one export icon. The summary does not state a retry after failed China check, so retry permission is unsupported; it does state only Company-controlled regions' export icons count. On success Company Balance gets £4 per such icon and Superintendent's family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company export icons do not count. The summary does not specify a separate China trade bonus beyond these payments.

When Governor General law passes, all Governors become pensioners; remove their overlays and partial Company ships; return Governor and Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and put ribbon overlay. No further Governors/overlays are created on conquest; printed Company symbols mark control. Governor General hires Presidents and uses Director's treasury/turn place; it is hired like Director and rolls attrition normally. On region loss, skip Governor Elimination.

Before Govern checks, Governor General adds £3 Balance per Company region. Govern may be attempted repeatedly, paying £1 from treasury per die, with no penalty, but at most one successful Govern per turn. Every rolled six adds one unrest to each Company region even if roll succeeds; a failure adds another unrest to every Company region. A success gains £1 per Company region and requires exactly one benefit for each region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China, put a regiment in any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any other office treasury (not own), adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple tax choices in one turn must place unrest in different regions.

In storm zone, roll once per player-owned ship: 1–2 no effect; 3–4 add fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. A sunk ship returns to its shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count in Eastern zone. Firm ships face storms in their strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.

When order closes, return any writer on newly closed order to owner's supply and flip a filled token to closed. If told to close in an already fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead; if none open, it also Cascades. A region may initiate a Cascade once per event tile but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.

Turmoil closes northernmost open order in the region shown by top stack; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall gives owners £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle first moves Elephant, then shuffles that event tile into remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards onto the top; if draw stack is empty, March last instead.

Leader: if top-stack region is sovereign, add one tower. If dominated, instead rebel there with printed explosion modifier. March Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace with Elephant on a border opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region, then Marches. With Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open every order there and remove its unrest, then March. Thus it moves afterward in either case.

For a non-Company Invasion, compare attacker's whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender's whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater, so equal strength fails. Success replaces defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; if taking capital, shatter its whole empire. If attacker has no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form. Failure costs attacker one tower. No separate rule is stated for a case where no empire flags remain beyond the no-free-flag result.

For a non-Company Rebellion, compare only rebel region's strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. Rebel must be strictly greater, so tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed); failure removes one tower from capital.

On Company Region Loss, Commander returns half family's trophies rounded up and Commander member returns to supply. Roll one die per officer in associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor by returning its office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies; remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (Foreign Invasion uses its specified tower strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to region with loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes all orders or Cascades if all closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing falls by regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, etc. If failure results, finish Events in India then score. Loss of a region does not automatically lose other Company regions; resolve each attack/defense separately.

After a successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches, it goes to top-stack region. In Company region put it fully inside. In dominated region point toward sovereign. In sovereign region point across shape-marked border on tile; if neighbor already dominated by actor, use first clockwise neighbor not so dominated. If all neighbors are dominated, use redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion rolls storm die to choose targets: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms means each target, none means top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength. Unrest does not increase primary attack strength or resulting tower level; use ordinary roll for both attack and half-roll tower strength rounded down. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove its flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down, and March in circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks apply; do not add normal primary Crisis unrest.

PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma laws, PM may stop or continue up to three; choose one revealed and discard the rest. A dilemma forces its own selection and ends drawing immediately. Before voting PM turns dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching selected law's bottom icon; that policy space determines target and consequence.

Tax: each family pays £1 to bank per owned target; unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman; fitted ship stays, and returned yard cannot be bought until ship returns; losing prize/luxury loses VP. If policy includes windows, additionally pay per window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return enterprise/prize member if unable. Bonus: bank pays family £1 per target it owns. Power: swap target's marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and moving clockwise, players cast votes by paying £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes. A card's votes can be used only once during the entire vote, across all rounds; rotate it when used until resolution. Players can cast further cash votes in later rounds if they still have family cash. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting. Support track is unlimited.

Yes: a supporter may later oppose; once a player has opposed, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes; largest opponent is Opposition Leader, and tied current holder keeps it. With recipient consent, votes can be cast for a player already opposed or committing to oppose, adding to that player's opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except forced use of “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

Pay upkeep separately for every family member on a prize, including on final turn. If unpaid, return member and lose printed VP. On final turn skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. Otherwise return writers to associated Presidencies; return filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted officers/regiments; exhaust active local alliances; advance turn and start London Season. Fitted player ships retain fatigue.

Each shareholder can make one extra London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of number of firms owned; actual spend is capped at the highest total dividend marker among firms they own a share in. No retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts may allow a higher printed-cost prize; otherwise normal retirement rules and prestige eligibility apply. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, with no display cards. Final scoring prohibits negotiations/promise calls.

Investments go from bank to firm's London treasury; trade proceeds go to India treasury. London pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India pays expenses and dividends. Expenses may use either/both treasuries. Remaining India money after dividends is swept to London. Firm shipyard fitting costs £3 from London to bank; purchases of player Company ships cost £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued paid to Shipping treasury. Family cash cannot be given into or taken from firm treasuries.

Firms phase follows Family share creation and precedes Hiring. Investment actions continue until nobody wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then strategies are selected. Firms' trade strategies are revealed and checks happen at the start of their associated Presidency operations, before any actions there. At Revenue, firms pay in initiative order, then other firms; ties by manager with most windows then clockwise from PM.

To fit a ship from a shipyard, the firm pays £3 from London treasury to bank and must have the shipyard owner's consent. A firm may buy a player-owned ship already in Company only with that owner's consent: £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paid to Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company ships or extra ships.

Only a player managing no firm at all may start hostile takeover; managing any other firm disqualifies them. Get consent from holders of majority of target firm's shares. Move target ships, money and shares to own charter; copy both cube positions. Former manager returns cubes and flips board back to family side.

Merger requires managers to negotiate and every shareholder to consent. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among those tied. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Negotiate transfers and any shares over ten with those owners' consent. Whole agreement is one binding immediate transfer; primary firm's Value/dividend track continues.

Hobnob is a strategy with no bid, trade or dividends. It retains previous dividend marker for retirement and exempts firm ships from storms. It still pays expenses. No additional retirement-marker effect is stated beyond retaining the previous marker.

Yes. Emergency investment follows normal Company-share/workshop contribution rules even when the ten-share limit prevents additional shares: contribute eligible share/workshop, bank adds £5 to London, pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space for each emergency investment. No new share is created beyond ten. The rule barring use of Company shares created this turn—even after trading them away—still applies.

Emergency merger rescue may merge with only one other firm; that other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and then cover endangered firm's unpaid expenses. Unlike voluntary multi-firm merger, the summary gives no requirement for every shareholder's consent, nor normal merger procedure; it describes this as alternative rescue. Details beyond these stated differences are unsupported.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. The summary refers to dissolution destinations below but gives destinations in the failing-firm dissolution rule: shares to Debtor's Prison, ships back to shipyards, charter board back to family side. It does not explicitly state whether voluntary dissolution uses those exact destinations. Invested workshops do not recover: they remain invested, including after firm failure.

If deregulated, each player totals VP from all their own firm shares across all firms, then rounds their own fractional total down (not per share, per firm or across players). Firm share rate: Value 1 −1 VP; 2 zero; 3–4 one-half; 5–7 one; 8–9 one-and-a-half; 10 two. Deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. These firm scores are before ordinary final scoring, regardless of Company failure. Ordinary Company share value is added if Company survives and subtracted if it failed; failure also gives 1 VP per uninvested workshop.

1710 starts turn 1 and ends turn 5, no Deregulation procedures. 1758 starts turn 3 and ends turn 7, and Deregulation can be voted in. 1813 starts turn 5 and ends turn 8, already deregulated. Long 1710 starts turn 1 and ends turn 8, with Deregulation available separately.

1710 begins Standing at £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection passed, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758 begins Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, each office treasury £4, Calico Acts passed, one regiment per Army and one Company ship in East Indian; it also has Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813 starts turn 5 with Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office £3; passed laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Add +2/−2 share-value token in Court; create China; place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies; return Governor General law to box; put its office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and have no Governors. Scenario card reverse sets exact India map; player-owned ships/offices are additionally from dealt setup cards.

Final Power awards are turn 1–3: first 3, second 1; turn 4–6: first 5, second 2; turn 7–8: first 8, second 4. In every band, a tied-first group each receives only the lower (second-place) award and nobody receives an additional award.

Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations spaces are £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; reset S sits above £10. Deregulation spaces: Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8 are lined (eligible for PM optional call); Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred (call is mandatory when either is there).

No. Designer ruling says unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its tower levels. Use the ordinary attack die both for strength and for the halved tower amount, rounded down. On success, close all orders; Cascade if already all closed. Region Loss does not add another order closure for Foreign Invasion because its added closure applies only to Invasion Crisis.

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection: reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud: played at start of Revenue; roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and receive bank cash equal only to actual Balance reduction, not an amount exceeding Balance. Public Demands Impeachment: return member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight: demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.

Shared setup sets Company Balance to £5 and family VP markers to zero. Put local alliances in their named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and use its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map; copy exact towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from reverse. Put Turn marker on scenario date and PM dial arm to matching date; scenario determines final turn.

Normal turn order: London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Special eligible Deregulation votes happen at very start before London Season. Skip London Season on the first turn of the game.

Retirements start with Chairman; if office vacant, the former Chairman goes first, then clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; they are not required to retire them. Pay printed cost, move pensioner/member to prize and gain its printed VP. Keep actual spending aside until London Season ends to set display order, then pay bank. Unused pensioners return to supplies and do not carry over.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that final dominated region.

Per firm share: Value 1 = −1 VP; Value 2 = 0; Values 3–4 = ½ VP; Values 5–7 = 1 VP; Values 8–9 = 1½ VP; Value 10 = 2 VP. Each player's combined fractional firm-share total is rounded down only after totaling their shares across all firms.
